report:
## Conclusion

Your health claim is well supported by evidence. The landmark randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (Pan et al., NEJM 2016) enrolled 200 HBeAg-positive mothers with HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL. Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) 300 mg daily started at gestational weeks 30–32 and continued through delivery reduced mother-to-child transmission (defined as infant HBsAg-positive at 6 months despite standard birth immunoprophylaxis) from 18% in controls to 5% in the TDF group. A subsequent JAMA noninferiority trial (2024) confirmed that initiating tenofovir at week 28 is effective and comparable to earlier initiation at week 16, supporting third-trimester start as adequate.

Safety data are reassuring: rates of obstetric complications, congenital anomalies, and infant adverse events did not differ significantly between tenofovir and placebo groups, and meta-analyses report no increase in birth defects or growth problems.

Guidelines reflect this evidence. The 2025 AASLD/IDSA chronic hepatitis B guideline recommends initiating TDF or tenofovir alafenamide at gestational week 28 for pregnant persons with HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL to prevent perinatal transmission, and notes therapy may be stopped at delivery or within four weeks postpartum with close follow-up. EASL similarly endorses third-trimester tenofovir for high-viremic mothers.

In short, multiple randomized trials and current specialty guidelines support that tenofovir begun in the third trimester in high-viral-load pregnant women with chronic hepatitis B safely and substantially reduces mother-to-child transmission.
